scope: Eight paired tail-sample feature comparisons and two full-data refit-policy comparisons

subsequent_source_verification.note: Verified against git show after the run started; original generation metadata remains unchanged.

limitations: One seed, one 500000-row tail sample, and one final-100000-row validation set
Transductive unsupervised features explicitly include validation and test interactions; no validation or test labels are used for fitting
The global-statistics comparison jointly changes vocabulary/count scope and self-counting policy
The larger-tree case jointly changes six training controls; its gain cannot be assigned to leaf count alone
The frequency case is compared with user_preferences under the same smaller-tree settings
Row gaps are order proxies, not elapsed seconds or guaranteed sessions
Single-run timing and peak RSS are descriptive; cache and host load are not controlled
Validation improvements do not establish platform gains or achievement of the requested AUC target

platform_submission.description: CS4304 transductive holdout: full unlabeled graph, row order, OOF target encoding, no refit

artifact_verification.feature_state_check: Cloud prediction successfully loaded the paired serialized state; local verification reads model headers and hashes without allocating the large pickle.

platform_submission.description: CS4304 transductive refit: full unlabeled graph, row order, OOF target encoding, all labeled rows

artifact_verification.feature_state_check: Cloud prediction successfully loaded the paired serialized state; local verification reads model headers and hashes without allocating the large pickle.

paired_full_data_comparison.interpretation: Refitting scores higher on both competition partitions in this controlled pair; the claim that skipping refit is necessarily better is not supported.

limitations: Sample validation uses the last 100000 rows; full-data validation uses the last 20 percent. Their AUCs are not directly comparable as feature gains.
All transductive variants include full train/test interactions without target labels in unsupervised statistics.
Row-order gaps are proxies rather than seconds or guaranteed sessions.
Platform targets are checked only after actual scoring; no historical leaderboard rank is inferred.
Single-run timing and peak RSS are descriptive, not controlled benchmarks.
